selectionReason: From this batch on, the proposal on issue 60 (comment 7058679348) governs the remaining rows: one supporting word article per kanji, Joyo rows first in source-row order, up to ten kanji per batch. The ten members are the first ten remaining Joyo rows. The article's word should carry one of JMdict's common-word tags news1, ichi1, spec1 or gai1; an untagged word needs a justification reviewed for its row, and the word's other kanji must already have cards or join the batch. At the freeze the author also counted news2 and spec2 as qualifying, so no row was flagged; 仙人 and 伯仲 carry only those two tags. The fix 7eaf5c24 then chose 甲乙 as the 乙 word, which also carries only news2 and spec2, without checking its other kanji 甲, which has no card and is not in the batch. Rechecked against the list, seven words carry a listed tag (丹念, 亜熱帯, 仁, 歌舞伎, 降伏, 伐採, 同伴). No reviewer had raised either error; the author disclosed both in the last confirmation round (confirm4-claude, confirm3-gpt and confirm2-grok), in statements that date both to the freeze, although 甲乙 entered in 7eaf5c24. ba44b280 replaced 甲乙 with 乙種 (JMdict 1862630, untagged), because 乙 alone (JMdict 1182940) can also be read おと (entry 2837087), 早乙女 and 乙女 are whole-word readings in the Joyo appendix that do not use オツ, and 乙種 is the first Joyo example for 乙, given by Digital Daijisen and Kanjipedia for the sense "second rank", with 種 already a card; 仙人 is kept because its only candidate with a listed tag is the city name 仙台 (spec1); 伯仲 is kept because 伯父 and 伯母 are tagged only for their whole-word readings おじ and おば, 伯爵 needs 爵, which has no card, and 画伯 is the alternative. All three review families accepted these row decisions. 伯 already had the declaring article 伯母さん, a whole-word reading that supports no 伯 reading. Each card quizzes exactly one on reading, the one its new article uses; every quizzed kun list is empty.

In both the only conflict was the derived manifest, regenerated with tools/build_manifest.py. integration/merge-proof.json and merge2-proof.json pass: every non-derived path equals one parent byte for byte (49,043 and 49,048 paths, none unmatched), none of the 32 batch runtime paths or 171 link targets was changed by main, no main-changed line mentions a batch kanji or word (the second merge's three images are binary and were not scanned), and the manifest lists every batch file; so, as for batches 144 and 155, no integration review was needed. ba44b280 is one commit on top of eafee44b, and the gates were rerun on it. review.execution: All twelve runs ran one after the other. Four Claude runs each once issued two read-only view calls at the same time: initial-claude at 13:17:46 UTC, confirm-claude at 16:28:09, confirm3-claude at 17:51:51 and confirm4-claude at 20:56:05 (times from the local session logs); their reports wrongly say that each response made one tool call. The other runs had at most one tool call in flight. From the confirm2 prompts on, the prompts also forbade combining several commands in one call; confirm3-claude disclosed three single PowerShell commands over several files, and confirm4-claude two single pipelines (a Compare-Object of two reads and a Get-FileHash over six paths). confirm-claude reports "51 reverse targets" for a cited range of 50 lines. initial-grok disclosed one recursive listing, but its scope audit shows eleven recursive commands over the packet or the repository snapshot and a recursive grep of the packet. The runtime compacted the context once in initial-claude, initial-gpt, confirm-claude, confirm-grok and confirm2-grok, and twice in initial-grok; the other six runs were not compacted (from the local session logs; provenance.json does not record compaction). Each confirmation was a fresh agent of the same model family, given the author's statement on its family's last report and allowed to read the original packet and its family's earlier reports; issue 60 asks for the original reviewers where possible. All three families' last confirmations are of ba44b280, which was committed (19:54:11 UTC) before any of them started; every run's actual model equals the requested one.

Under the batch rule each card quizzes the one on reading its new article uses (丹 タン, 乙 オツ, 亜 ア, 仁 ジン, 仙 セン, 伎 キ, 伏 フク, 伐 バツ, 伯 ハク, 伴 ハン); the other readings are listed, not quizzed. 伎 わざおぎ and 伐 ハツ, カ, ボチ and そむ.く have no checked JMdict example and are labelled source-only on the cards.
The ten cards declare 86 exclusions. The only exclusion between two new cards is 亜/乙, declared on 亜; the app's QuizBuilder applies an exclusion in both directions.
Each mnemonic is a modern-shape memory aid, labelled on the card as not etymology; component and stroke statements follow the pinned KanjiVG revision.

The scope audits do not attribute reads made through shell commands or Python, so they can list files as unread that the reports say were read; some of their out-of-scope flags are false positives (base paths, the reports folder, strings parsed out of JSON).

Several judgments rest partly on live reads of Kanjipedia, Digital Daijisen (Weblio), Kotobank, Jisho, Takoboto and jpdb pages, not on pinned copies in the packets; EDRDG's JMdictDB pages ask for a password, so the reviewers checked JMdict ids against the packets' extracts and third-party mirrors.
The confirmation reviewers did not rerun the gates; they judged the check outputs that the author ran on each revised snapshot and included in their packets.

Each confirmation ran as a new agent of the same model family, with no memory of its own earlier reading; Grok was not asked to confirm a7cc61e2 on its own, and confirm2-grok reviewed its Metadata ids at ba44b280. Issue 60 asks for corrections to be confirmed with the original reviewers where possible; as in batches 150-155, each confirmation ran as a new agent instead.

Facet assignment: the repository's review rule for new word articles asks for three reviewers of different families, one each for correctness, consistency and quiz safety, and comprehensibility; here each reviewer covered all four facets with an assigned emphasis (Claude: correctness and scoped coverage; GPT: consistency, quiz safety and comprehensibility; Grok: comprehensibility). The issue 60 proposal named a two-family review; the author added Grok under the repository rule; no reply to the proposal has been posted on issue 60 yet.
